title: HTML Structure as a Page Blueprint: Analogy and Limits
learningObjectives: Explain HTML's role in your own words
Distinguish the roles of HTML, CSS and JavaScript

understand.concept: HTML structure can be compared to a building plan: it identifies sections and their relationships. Headings, navigation, main content and footer each communicate a role. The analogy is limited because HTML is semantic document markup, not a visual floor plan; CSS determines much of the visual layout.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding HTML helps you choose elements that make pages meaningful, maintainable and easier for different users and tools to interpret.
understand.history: HTML grew from the early linked-document web. Verify exact historical milestones against authoritative standards sources before publishing dates.
understand.analogy: HTML is like a plan that organizes the roles of parts in a document.
understand.analogyLimit: HTML is not a visual design tool; CSS controls visual presentation.

explain.narrative: HTML structure can be compared to a building plan: it identifies sections and their relationships. Headings, navigation, main content and footer each communicate a role. The analogy is limited because HTML is semantic document markup, not a visual floor plan; CSS determines much of the visual layout.

examples.explanation: The header, main and footer elements identify meaningful page regions. They describe structure and purpose, not colours or visual positioning; CSS controls visual presentation.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser displays the meaningful HTML content.

practise.guidedTask: Identify each element and attribute in the example and explain its role.
practise.independentTask: Write your own small HTML fragment using the same concept and open it in a browser.
hints: Separate HTML structure, CSS presentation and JavaScript behaviour.
A visible page alone does not guarantee valid markup.
